scheme_name: "Protected Cultivation" Component of "Establishment of New Gardens (Area Expansion)" Scheme
description:
The "Protected Cultivation" component of the "Establishment of New Gardens (Area Expansion)" scheme is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing horticultural production through the use of protected cultivation techniques.

This scheme was launched in 2014 under the National Horticulture Mission.

The primary objective of this component is to promote the establishment of new gardens using advanced horticultural practices.

The scheme specifically aims to increase the area under protected cultivation by 20 percent by the year 2025.

The government has set a target to cover approximately 20,000 hectares under protected cultivation across the country.

The benefits of this scheme include increased productivity of horticultural crops.

Protected cultivation can lead to a yield increase of 30 to 50 percent compared to traditional farming methods.

Farmers can receive financial assistance of up to INR 2.5 lakh per hectare for establishing protected structures.

The assistance is provided at a subsidy rate of 50 percent for small and marginal farmers.

For larger farmers, the subsidy rate is 40 percent.

The scheme covers various types of protected structures including greenhouses, shade nets, and polyhouses.

Eligible crops under this scheme include vegetables, flowers, and fruits.

The eligibility criteria for farmers include being a resident of India.

Farmers must also possess a minimum landholding of 0.5 hectares.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years.

The income criteria require that the farmer's annual income does not exceed INR 2 lakh.

Farmers must also have basic knowledge of horticultural practices or must undergo training.

The application process involves several steps.

First, interested farmers must visit the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

They need to fill out the application form available online.

Farmers must submit proof of land ownership along with the application.

A copy of the farmer's Aadhaar card is also required for identity verification.

In addition, a bank account statement is needed to facilitate subsidy disbursement.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the respective state horticulture department.

The state department conducts a field verification to assess the eligibility of the applicant.

If approved, the farmer receives a sanction order detailing the subsidy amount.

The disbursement of funds is made directly to the farmer's bank account.

The timeline for the entire application process can vary.

Typically, the review and approval process takes about 30 to 45 days.

Farmers are encouraged to apply during the sowing season to maximize benefits.

The scheme is implemented through the Department of Horticulture in each state.

Each state has its own horticulture department that oversees the implementation.

Farmers can contact their local horticulture office for assistance.

The contact details of these offices can be found on the official state government websites.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to increase the income of farmers.

The government aims to double farmers' income by the year 2022.

Protected cultivation is seen as a key strategy to achieve this goal.

The scheme also promotes sustainable agricultural practices.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt eco-friendly methods in protected cultivation.

The use of technology in farming is also a focus area.

Farmers can utilize drip irrigation and fertigation systems to optimize resource use.

The scheme has been well-received in various states.

States like Maharashtra and Karnataka have reported significant increases in horticultural production.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crore for this scheme over the next five years.

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted regularly.

The Ministry of Agriculture collects data on the number of beneficiaries and area covered.

This data is used to assess the impact of the scheme on horticultural productivity.

The scheme also aims to create employment opportunities in rural areas.

It is expected to generate around 1 million jobs in the horticulture sector.

Farmers are also encouraged to form cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power.

The cooperative model helps in collective marketing of produce.

Farmers can also access better technology and training through cooperatives.

The scheme is aligned with the Prime Minister's vision of "Atmanirbhar Bharat."

This vision emphasizes self-reliance in agriculture and food security.

The government is also promoting research and development in horticulture.

Collaboration with agricultural universities is encouraged to improve practices.

Farmers can participate in training programs organized by these institutions.

The scheme also includes provisions for post-harvest management.

Farmers are trained in techniques to reduce post-harvest losses.

The focus is on improving the shelf life of horticultural produce.

The government is also facilitating market access for farmers.

Online platforms are being developed for direct selling of produce.

Farmers can sell their products directly to consumers.

This reduces the dependency on middlemen.

The scheme is expected to contribute significantly to the GDP of the agricultural sector.

The horticulture sector has been growing at a rate of 5 to 6 percent annually.

The government aims to further boost this growth through initiatives like this scheme.

Overall, the "Protected Cultivation" component of the "Establishment of New Gardens (Area Expansion)" scheme represents a significant step towards modernizing Indian agriculture.

It aims to empower farmers through financial assistance and training.

The focus on protected cultivation is expected to lead to sustainable agricultural practices.

This will ultimately benefit the economy and improve food security in the country.
